questions.text:
Let $A=\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $(x, y)\in R$ if and only if $\max\{x, y\}\in\{3, 4\}$. Then among the statements
$(S_1)$ : The number of elements in $R$ is 18, and
$(S_2)$ : The relation $R$ is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
questions.sol:
Pairs with maximum 3: $4^2-3^2=7$; pairs with maximum 4: $5^2-4^2=9$. So $n(R)=16$ and $(S_1)$ is false.
The condition is symmetric in $x, y$, so $R$ is symmetric. $(0, 0)\notin R$, so it is not reflexive. $(1, 3), (3, 1)\in R$ but $(1, 1)\notin R$, so it is not transitive. $(S_2)$ is true.

questions.text: The sum of the squares of the roots of $|x-2|^2+|x-2|-2=0$ and the squares of the roots of $x^2-2|x-3|-5=0$, is
questions.sol:
First equation: with $t=|x-2|\ge0$, $t^2+t-2=0$ gives $t=1$, so $x=1, 3$; squares add to $10$.
Second equation: for $x\ge3$, $x^2-2x+1=0$ gives $x=1$, rejected. For $x<3$, $x^2+2x-11=0$ gives $x=-1\pm2\sqrt3$, both less than 3; squares add to $(-2)^2-2(-11)=26$.
Total $=10+26=36$.

questions.text: Let $A=\left\{\theta\in[0, 2\pi]:1+10\,\mathrm{Re}\left(\dfrac{2\cos\theta+i\sin\theta}{\cos\theta-3i\sin\theta}\right)=0\right\}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{\theta\in A}\theta^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Multiply numerator and denominator by $\cos\theta+3i\sin\theta$: the real part is $\dfrac{2\cos^2\theta-3\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta+9\sin^2\theta}$.
The condition becomes $\cos^2\theta+9\sin^2\theta+20\cos^2\theta-30\sin^2\theta=0$, i.e. $\tan^2\theta=1$.
$\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}$, so $\sum\theta^2=\dfrac{\pi^2}{16}(1+9+25+49)=\dfrac{21}{4}\pi^2$.

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2+p & 2+p+q\\ 4 & 6+2p & 8+3p+2q\\ 6 & 12+3p & 20+6p+3q\end{bmatrix}$. If $\det(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}(3A)))=2^m\cdot3^n$, $m, n\in\mathbb{N}$, then $m+n$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$R_2\to R_2-2R_1$, $R_3\to R_3-3R_1$ give rows $(0, 2, 4+p)$ and $(0, 6, 14+3p)$, so $\det A=2\left[2(14+3p)-6(4+p)\right]=8$.
For order 3, $\det(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}M))=(\det M)^4$, and $\det(3A)=27\times8=2^3\cdot3^3$.
So the value is $2^{12}\cdot3^{12}$: $m+n=24$.

questions.text: Let $\alpha$ be a solution of $x^2+x+1=0$, and for some $a$ and $b$ in $\mathbb{R}$, $\begin{bmatrix}4 & a & b\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 16 & 13\\ -1 & -1 & 2\\ -2 & -14 & -8\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$. If $\dfrac{4}{\alpha^4}+\dfrac{m}{\alpha^a}+\dfrac{n}{\alpha^b}=3$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Columns: $4-a-2b=0$ and $64-a-14b=0$ give $b=5$, $a=-6$ (the third column, $52+2a-8b=0$, checks).
$\alpha$ is a non-real cube root of unity, so $\alpha^4=\alpha$, $\alpha^{-6}=1$, $\alpha^5=\alpha^2$.
$\dfrac4\alpha+m+\dfrac{n}{\alpha^2}=4\alpha^2+m+n\alpha=3$. With $\alpha^2=-1-\alpha$: $(m-4)+(n-4)\alpha=3$, so $n=4$, $m=7$ and $m+n=11$.

questions.text:
If $\dfrac{1}{1^4}+\dfrac{1}{2^4}+\dfrac{1}{3^4}+\ldots\infty=\dfrac{\pi^4}{90}$,
$\dfrac{1}{1^4}+\dfrac{1}{3^4}+\dfrac{1}{5^4}+\ldots\infty=\alpha$,
$\dfrac{1}{2^4}+\dfrac{1}{4^4}+\dfrac{1}{6^4}+\ldots\infty=\beta$,
then $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Let $S=\dfrac{\pi^4}{90}$. The even terms are $\beta=\dfrac{1}{2^4}S=\dfrac{S}{16}$.
$\alpha=S-\beta=\dfrac{15S}{16}$, so $\dfrac\alpha\beta=15$.

questions.sol: Choose any 3 of the 12 points and remove the choices lying on the line of 5: ${}^{12}C_3-{}^5C_3=220-10=210$.

questions.text: The number of integral terms in the expansion of $\left(5^{\frac12}+7^{\frac18}\right)^{1016}$ is
questions.sol:
$T_{r+1}={}^{1016}C_r\,5^{\frac{1016-r}{2}}\,7^{\frac r8}$ is an integer when $8\mid r$ (then $1016-r$ is even too).
$r=0, 8, \ldots, 1016$: $\dfrac{1016}{8}+1=128$ terms.

questions.text: If $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A)=0.7$, $P(B)=0.4$ and $P(A\cap\bar{B})=0.5$, where $\bar{B}$ denotes the complement of $B$, then $P\left(B\,|\,(A\cup\bar{B})\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$P(A\cap B)=0.7-0.5=0.2$ and $P(A\cup\bar B)=0.7+0.6-0.5=0.8$.
$B\cap(A\cup\bar B)=A\cap B$, so the required probability is $\dfrac{0.2}{0.8}=\dfrac14$.

questions.text: A line passing through the point $P(a, 0)$ makes an acute angle $\alpha$ with the positive $x$-axis. Let this line be rotated about the point $P$ through an angle $\dfrac{\alpha}{2}$ in the clock-wise direction. If in the new position, the slope of the line is $2-\sqrt3$ and its distance from the origin is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, then the value of $3a^2\tan^2\alpha-2\sqrt3$ is
questions.sol:
After the rotation the line makes angle $\dfrac\alpha2$ with the $x$-axis, and $\tan\dfrac\alpha2=2-\sqrt3$ gives $\dfrac\alpha2=15^\circ$, $\alpha=30^\circ$.
Distance of the origin from a line through $(a, 0)$ at $15^\circ$: $|a|\sin15^\circ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, so $a^2=\dfrac{1}{2\sin^215^\circ}=\dfrac{1}{1-\cos30^\circ}=2(2+\sqrt3)$.
$3a^2\tan^2\alpha-2\sqrt3=3\cdot2(2+\sqrt3)\cdot\dfrac13-2\sqrt3=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $a$ be the length of a side of a square OABC with O being the origin. Its side OA makes an acute angle $\alpha$ with the positive $x$-axis and the equations of its diagonals are $(\sqrt3+1)x+(\sqrt3-1)y=0$ and $(\sqrt3-1)x-(\sqrt3+1)y+8\sqrt3=0$. Then $a^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The first diagonal passes through O, so the second is AC. The distance of O from AC is half a diagonal, $\dfrac{a}{\sqrt2}$.
Distance $=\dfrac{8\sqrt3}{\sqrt{(\sqrt3-1)^2+(\sqrt3+1)^2}}=\dfrac{8\sqrt3}{\sqrt8}=2\sqrt6$.
$a=2\sqrt6\cdot\sqrt2=4\sqrt3$, so $a^2=48$.

questions.text: Let the ellipse $3x^2+py^2=4$ pass through the centre $C$ of the circle $x^2+y^2-2x-4y-11=0$ of radius $r$. Let $f_1, f_2$ be the focal distances of the point $C$ on the ellipse. Then $6f_1f_2-r$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$C=(1, 2)$ and $r=\sqrt{1+4+11}=4$. Then $3+4p=4$, so $p=\dfrac14$ and the ellipse is $\dfrac{x^2}{4/3}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$ (major axis along $y$, semi-major axis 4).
$e^2=1-\dfrac{4/3}{16}=\dfrac{11}{12}$. Focal distances of $(1, 2)$: $4\pm2e$, so $f_1f_2=16-4e^2=\dfrac{37}{3}$.
$6f_1f_2-r=74-4=70$.

questions.text: The value of $\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+\tan^2(2)}-1}{\tan(2)}\right)-\cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+\tan^2\left(\frac12\right)}+1}{\tan\left(\frac12\right)}\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\sqrt{1+\tan^2x}=|\sec x|$. Since 2 rad lies in the second quadrant, $|\sec2|=-\sec2$, and the first argument is $\dfrac{-\sec2-1}{\tan2}=-\dfrac{1+\cos2}{\sin2}=-\cot1$. So the first term is $\cot^{-1}(-\cot1)=\pi-1$.
For $\dfrac12$ rad, the second argument is $\dfrac{1+\cos\frac12}{\sin\frac12}=\cot\dfrac14$, so the second term is $\dfrac14$.
Value $=\pi-1-\dfrac14=\pi-\dfrac54$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$. Let $\hat{c}$ be a unit vector in the plane of the vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ and be perpendicular to $\vec{a}$. Then such a vector $\hat{c}$ is :
questions.sol:
Remove from $\vec b$ its component along $\vec a$: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=3$, $|\vec a|^2=6$, so $\vec b-\dfrac12\vec a=\dfrac32\hat i-\dfrac32\hat k$.
Unit vectors along it: $\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}(\hat i-\hat k)$; option (3) is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}(-\hat i+\hat k)$. (Options (1), (2) and (4) are perpendicular to $\vec a$ but not in the plane: they are not perpendicular to $\vec a\times\vec b=-3(\hat i-\hat j+\hat k)$.)
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the values of $\lambda$ for which the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-\lambda}{3}=\dfrac{y-4}{4}=\dfrac{z-5}{5}$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}$ be $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$. Then the radius of the circle passing through the points $(0, 0)$, $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2)$ and $(\lambda_2, \lambda_1)$ is
questions.sol:
$(2, 3, 4)\times(3, 4, 5)=(-1, 2, -1)$, of length $\sqrt6$. The join of $(1, 2, 3)$ and $(\lambda, 4, 5)$ is $(\lambda-1, 2, 2)$.
Distance $=\dfrac{|-(\lambda-1)+4-2|}{\sqrt6}=\dfrac{|3-\lambda|}{\sqrt6}=\dfrac1{\sqrt6}$, so $\lambda=2, 4$.
Circle $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy=0$ through $(2, 4)$ and $(4, 2)$: $20+4g+8f=0$, $20+8g+4f=0$, so $g=f=-\dfrac53$ and $r=\sqrt{g^2+f^2}=\dfrac{5\sqrt2}{3}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\left(\frac{\tan^{-1}x+\log_e\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}-2x}{x^5}\right)=\frac25$
Statement II : $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\left(x^{\frac{2}{1-x}}\right)=\frac{1}{e^2}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $\tan^{-1}x=x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{x^5}{5}-\cdots$ and $\log_e\sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}}=x+\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{x^5}{5}+\cdots$, so the numerator is $\dfrac{2x^5}{5}+\cdots$ and the limit is $\dfrac25$. True.
Statement II: the limit is $\exp\left(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1}\frac{2\log_e x}{1-x}\right)=e^{-2}$. True.

questions.text: Let the function $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{3}{x}+3$, $x\ne0$ be strictly increasing in $(-\infty, \alpha_1)\cup(\alpha_2, \infty)$ and strictly decreasing in $(\alpha_3, \alpha_4)\cup(\alpha_4, \alpha_5)$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{5}\alpha_i^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$f'(x)=\dfrac13-\dfrac{3}{x^2}$, positive for $|x|>3$ and negative for $0<|x|<3$.
Increasing on $(-\infty, -3)\cup(3, \infty)$, decreasing on $(-3, 0)\cup(0, 3)$: $\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_5=-3, 3, -3, 0, 3$.
$\sum\alpha_i^2=9+9+9+0+9=36$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)$ be a positive function and $I_1=\displaystyle\int_{-\frac12}^{1}2x\,f\left(2x(1-2x)\right)dx$ and $I_2=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2}f\left(x(1-x)\right)dx$. Then the value of $\dfrac{I_2}{I_1}$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Put $t=2x$ in $I_1$: $I_1=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2}t\,f\left(t(1-t)\right)dt=\dfrac12J$.
Replacing $t$ by $1-t$ (the limits $-1, 2$ add to 1) leaves $t(1-t)$ unchanged, so $J=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2}(1-t)f\left(t(1-t)\right)dt$ and $2J=I_2$.
$I_1=\dfrac{I_2}{4}$, so $\dfrac{I_2}{I_1}=4$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The integral $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{\frac32}\left(\left|\pi^2x\sin(\pi x)\right|\right)dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
An antiderivative of $\pi^2x\sin\pi x$ is $F(x)=\sin\pi x-\pi x\cos\pi x$, with $F(0)=0$, $F(1)=\pi$, $F\left(\frac32\right)=-1$.
On $[-1, 1]$ the integrand $x\sin\pi x$ is even and non-negative: contribution $2F(1)=2\pi$.
On $\left[1, \frac32\right]$ it is negative: contribution $F(1)-F\left(\frac32\right)=\pi+1$.
Total $=1+3\pi$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f(x)=x-1$ and $g(x)=e^x$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$. If $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\left(e^{-2\sqrt{x}}g\left(f\left(f(x)\right)\right)-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x}}\right)$, $y(0)=0$, then $y(1)$ is
questions.sol:
$g(f(f(x)))=e^{x-2}$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{y}{\sqrt x}=e^{x-2-2\sqrt x}$.
Integrating factor $e^{2\sqrt x}$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(ye^{2\sqrt x}\right)=e^{x-2}$, so $ye^{2\sqrt x}=e^{x-2}-e^{-2}$ (using $y(0)=0$).
$y(1)=e^{-2}\left(e^{-1}-e^{-2}\right)=\dfrac{e-1}{e^4}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the domain of the function $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\right)$ be $[\alpha, \beta]$ and the domain of $g(x)=\log_2\left(2-6\log_{27}(2x+5)\right)$ be $(\gamma, \delta)$. Then $|7(\alpha+\beta)+4(\gamma+\delta)|$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\le1\iff\dfrac{x+12}{3x-7}\le0\iff-12\le x<\dfrac73$; $\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\ge-1\iff\dfrac{7x-2}{3x-7}\ge0\iff x\le\dfrac27$ or $x>\dfrac73$. So the domain is $\left[-12, \dfrac27\right]$ and $7(\alpha+\beta)=-82$.
$g$: $\log_{27}(2x+5)<\dfrac13$, i.e. $0<2x+5<3$, so $-\dfrac52<x<-1$ and $4(\gamma+\delta)=-14$.
$|-82-14|=96$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The product of the last two digits of $(1919)^{1919}$ is __________
questions.sol:
Work modulo 100: $1919^{1919}\equiv19^{1919}$. $19^2\equiv61$, $19^4\equiv21$, $19^5\equiv399\equiv-1$, so $19^{10}\equiv1$.
$19^{1919}=\left(19^{10}\right)^{191}\cdot19^9\equiv19^5\cdot19^4\equiv-21\equiv79$.
Last two digits 7 and 9: product $63$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $r$ be the radius of the circle, which touches $x$-axis at point $(a, 0)$, $a<0$ and the parabola $y^2=9x$ at the point $(4, 6)$. Then $r$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
The tangent to the parabola at $(4, 6)$ is $6y=\dfrac92(x+4)$, slope $\dfrac34$; the normal has direction $(-3, 4)$.
The centre is $(4, 6)\pm\dfrac r5(-3, 4)$ and, as the circle touches the $x$-axis at $(a, 0)$, it is $(a, \pm r)$.
Taking $+$: $6+\dfrac{4r}{5}=r$ gives $r=30$ and $a=4-18=-14<0$. The other choices give $a>0$ or $r<0$. So $r=30$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the area of the triangle formed by the lines $x+2=y-1=z$, $\dfrac{x-3}{5}=\dfrac{y}{-1}=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x}{-3}=\dfrac{y-3}{3}=\dfrac{z-2}{1}$ be $A$. Then $A^2$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Solving in pairs, the lines meet at $P(-2, 1, 0)$ (first and second), $Q(0, 3, 2)$ (first and third) and $R(3, 0, 1)$ (second and third).
$\vec{PQ}=(2, 2, 2)$, $\vec{PR}=(5, -1, 1)$, $\vec{PQ}\times\vec{PR}=(4, 8, -12)$, with $|\cdot|^2=224$.
$A^2=\dfrac{224}{4}=56$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the area of the bounded region $\{(x, y): 0\le9x\le y^2, y\ge3x-6\}$ be $A$. Then $6A$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
The set lies in $x\ge0$, outside the parabola $y^2=9x$ and above the line $y=3x-6$. The part with $y\ge0$ is unbounded; the bounded part lies below the $x$-axis, between $x=0$, the line and the lower branch $y=-3\sqrt x$, which meet at $(1, -3)$.
$A=\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(-3\sqrt x-(3x-6)\right)dx=-2-\frac32+6=\frac52$.
$6A=15$.

questions.text: A quantity Q is formulated as $X^{-2}Y^{+\frac32}Z^{-\frac25}$. X, Y and Z are independent parameters which have fractional errors of 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5, respectively in measurement. The maximum fractional error of Q is
questions.sol: Maximum fractional error $=2(0.1)+\dfrac32(0.2)+\dfrac25(0.5)=0.2+0.3+0.2=0.7$.

questions.text: A body of mass 2 kg moving with velocity of $\vec{v}_{in}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ ms$^{-1}$ enters into a constant force field of 6N directed along positive z-axis. If the body remains in the field for a period of $\dfrac53$ seconds, then velocity of the body when it emerges from force field is.
questions.sol:
Acceleration $=\dfrac62=3$ m s$^{-2}$ along $+z$; in $\dfrac53$ s the body gains $v_z=5$ m/s.
The $x$ and $y$ components are unchanged: $\vec v=3\hat i+4\hat j+5\hat k$.

questions.text: A rod of linear mass density '$\lambda$' and length 'L' is bent to form a ring of radius 'R'. Moment of inertia of ring about any of its diameter is.
questions.sol: $M=\lambda L$ and $R=\dfrac{L}{2\pi}$. About a diameter $I=\dfrac{MR^2}{2}=\dfrac{\lambda L}{2}\cdot\dfrac{L^2}{4\pi^2}=\dfrac{\lambda L^3}{8\pi^2}$.

questions.text: A block of mass 2 kg is attached to one end of a massless spring whose other end is fixed at a wall. The spring-mass system moves on a frictionless horizontal table. The spring's natural length is 2 m and spring constant is 200 N/m. The block is pushed such that the length of the spring becomes 1 m and then released. At distance $x$ m ($x<2$) from the wall, the speed of the block will be
questions.sol:
The block performs SHM about $x=2$ m with amplitude 1 m and $\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac{200}{2}}=10$ rad/s.
At displacement $2-x$ the speed is $\omega\sqrt{A^2-(2-x)^2}=10\left[1-(2-x)^2\right]^{1/2}$ m/s.

questions.text: Two balls with same mass and initial velocity, are projected at different angles in such a way that maximum height reached by first ball is 8 times higher than that of the second ball. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are the total flying times of first and second ball, respectively, then the ratio of $T_1$ and $T_2$ is
questions.sol:
$H=\dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$ and $T=\dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$, so $T\propto\sqrt H$ for the same $u$.
$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}=\sqrt8=2\sqrt2$.

questions.text: A 3 m long wire of radius 3 mm shows an extension of 0.1 mm when loaded vertically by a mass of 50 kg in an experiment to determine Young's modulus. The value of Young's modulus of the wire as per this experiment is $P\times10^{11}$ Nm$^{-2}$, where the value of P is: (Take $g=3\pi$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol: $Y=\dfrac{FL}{A\,\Delta L}=\dfrac{50\times3\pi\times3}{\pi(3\times10^{-3})^2\times10^{-4}}=\dfrac{450}{9\times10^{-10}}=5\times10^{11}$ N m$^{-2}$, so $P=5$.

questions.text:
Water falls from a height of 200 m into a pool. Calculate the rise in temperature of the water assuming no heat dissipation from the water in the pool.
(Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$, specific heat of water $=4200$ J/(kg K))
questions.sol: All the potential energy becomes heat: $mgh=mc\,\Delta T$, so $\Delta T=\dfrac{gh}{c}=\dfrac{2000}{4200}\approx0.48$ K.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A monoatomic gas having $\gamma=\dfrac53$ is stored in a thermally insulated container and the gas is suddenly compressed to $\left(\dfrac18\right)^{th}$ of its initial volume. The ratio of final pressure and initial pressure is:
($\gamma$ is the ratio of specific heats of the gas at constant pressure and at constant volume)
questions.sol:
Sudden compression in an insulated container is adiabatic: $PV^\gamma$ is constant.
$\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}=8^{5/3}=2^5=32$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two strings with circular cross section and made of same material, are stretched to have same amount of tension. A transverse wave is then made to pass through both the strings. The velocity of the wave in the first string having the radius of cross section R is $v_1$, and that in the other string having radius of cross section R/2 is $v_2$. Then $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}=$
questions.sol:
Speed on a stretched string $v=\sqrt{T/\mu}$ with $\mu=\rho\pi r^2$, so $v\propto\dfrac1r$ for equal tension and material.
$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}=\dfrac{R}{R/2}=2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : Work done in moving a test charge between two points inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is zero, no matter which path is chosen.
Reason R : Electrostatic potential inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is constant and is same as that on the surface of the shell.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
Inside the shell the field is zero, so the potential is constant and equal to its surface value (R true).
Work $=q\,\Delta V=0$ between any two inside points, whatever the path (A true), and this follows directly from R.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
An infinitely long wire has uniform linear charge density $\lambda=2$ nC/m. The net flux through a Gaussian cube of side length $\sqrt3$ cm, if the wire passes through any two corners of the cube, that are maximally displaced from each other, would be $x$ Nm$^2$C$^{-1}$, where $x$ is:
[Neglect any edge effects and use $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}=9\times10^9$ SI units]
questions.sol:
The wire runs along a body diagonal, of length $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3=3$ cm, so the enclosed charge is $2\times10^{-9}\times0.03=6\times10^{-11}$ C.
Flux $=\dfrac{q}{\varepsilon_0}=6\times10^{-11}\times4\pi\times9\times10^9=2.16\pi$ N m$^2$ C$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Electric charge is transferred to an irregular metallic disk as shown in figure. If $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$, $\sigma_3$ and $\sigma_4$ are charge densities at given points then, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
A. $\sigma_1>\sigma_3$ ; $\sigma_2=\sigma_4$
B. $\sigma_1>\sigma_2$ ; $\sigma_3>\sigma_4$
C. $\sigma_1>\sigma_3>\sigma_2=\sigma_4$
D. $\sigma_1<\sigma_3<\sigma_2=\sigma_4$
E. $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=\sigma_3=\sigma_4$
questions.note: The figure does not make it obvious that the lower end ($\sigma_3$) is more curved than the sides; NTA's final key (A, B and C) takes $\sigma_3>\sigma_2=\sigma_4$.
questions.sol:
On a charged conductor the surface charge density is largest where the surface is most sharply curved (smallest radius of curvature).
The pointed top gives the largest $\sigma_1$; the points at the two sides are alike, so $\sigma_2=\sigma_4$; the lower end is more curved than the sides, so $\sigma_3>\sigma_2$.
Hence $\sigma_1>\sigma_3>\sigma_2=\sigma_4$, and A, B and C are all correct.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two metal spheres of radius R and 3R have same surface charge density $\sigma$. If they are brought in contact and then separated, the surface charge density on smaller and bigger sphere becomes $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, respectively . The ratio $\dfrac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}$ is
questions.sol:
After contact the spheres are at the same potential: $\dfrac{q_1}{R}=\dfrac{q_2}{3R}$.
With $q=4\pi r^2\sigma$: $\sigma_1R=\sigma_2(3R)$, so $\dfrac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Figure shows a current carrying square loop ABCD of edge length is '$a$' lying in a plane. If the resistance of the ABC part is r and that of ADC part is 2r, then the magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at centre of the square loop is
questions.sol:
The current divides inversely as the resistances: $i_1=\dfrac{2I}{3}$ through ABC and $i_2=\dfrac I3$ through ADC.
One side carrying $i$ gives at the centre $\dfrac{\mu_0i}{4\pi(a/2)}(2\sin45^\circ)=\dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0i}{2\pi a}$.
The two halves give opposite fields: $B=2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0}{2\pi a}(i_1-i_2)=\dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0}{\pi a}\cdot\dfrac I3=\dfrac{\sqrt2\mu_0I}{3\pi a}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The amplitude and phase of a wave that is formed by the superposition of two harmonic travelling waves, $y_1(x, t)=4\sin(kx-\omega t)$ and $y_2(x, t)=2\sin\left(kx-\omega t+\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$, are:
(Take the angular frequency of initial waves same as $\omega$)
questions.sol:
$A^2=4^2+2^2+2(4)(2)\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=12$, so $A=2\sqrt3$.
$\tan\phi=\dfrac{2\sin(2\pi/3)}{4+2\cos(2\pi/3)}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}$, so $\phi=\dfrac\pi6$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A concave-convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and the radii of curvature of its surfaces are 30 cm and 20 cm, respectively. The concave surface is upwards and is filled with a liquid of refractive index 1.3. The focal length of the liquid–glass combination will be
questions.sol:
Glass meniscus (concave face radius 30 cm, convex face radius 20 cm): $\dfrac1{f_g}=0.5\left(\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{30}\right)=\dfrac1{120}$.
The liquid in the concave face forms a plano-convex lens of radius 30 cm: $\dfrac1{f_l}=0.3\times\dfrac1{30}=\dfrac1{100}$.
In contact: $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1{120}+\dfrac1{100}=\dfrac{11}{600}$, so $f=\dfrac{600}{11}$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the source is white light. One of the slits is covered by red filter and another by a green filter. In this case
options: there shall be alternate interference fringes of red and green.
there shall be an interference pattern for red distinct from that for green.
there shall be no interference fringes.
there shall be an interference pattern, where each fringe's pattern center is green and outer edges is red.
questions.sol: Light from the two slits now has different frequencies, so the two sources are not coherent and no steady pattern of fringes forms; the screen is simply illuminated by both colours.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A convex lens of focal length 30 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. An object is placed at 20 cm to the left of this lens system. The distance of the image from the lens in cm is __________.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1F=\dfrac1{30}-\dfrac1{20}=-\dfrac1{60}$, so $F=-60$ cm.
With $u=-20$ cm: $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1F+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{60}-\dfrac1{20}=-\dfrac1{15}$, so $v=-15$ cm: the image is 15 cm from the lens.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For a nucleus of mass number A and radius R, the mass density of nucleus can be represented as
questions.sol: $R=R_0A^{1/3}$, so the volume is proportional to $A$, as is the mass. Their ratio, the density, does not depend on $A$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The output voltage in the following circuit is
(Consider ideal diode case)
questions.sol:
The output node is joined to +5 V through the resistor. $D_2$ has its anode at the node and its cathode at earth, so it conducts and, being ideal, holds the node at 0 V.
$D_1$ then has 0 V on its anode and +5 V on its cathode: it is reverse biased and carries no current.
$V_{out}=0$ V.

questions.text: A cube having a side of 10 cm with unknown mass and 200 gm mass were hung at two ends of an uniform rigid rod of 27 cm long. The rod along with masses was placed on a wedge keeping the distance between wedge point and 200 gm weight as 25 cm. Initially the masses were not at balance. A beaker is placed beneath the unknown mass and water is added slowly to it. At given point the masses were in balance and half volume of the unknown mass was inside the water. (Take the density of unknown mass is more than that of the water, the mass did not absorb water and water density is 1 gm/cm$^3$.) The unknown mass is __________ kg.
questions.note: The rod's mass is not given; the answer 3 (NTA's final key) is obtained by neglecting the rod's weight.
questions.sol:
The cube hangs 2 cm from the wedge and the 200 g mass 25 cm from it. Half the cube ($500$ cm$^3$) is in water, so the upthrust equals the weight of 500 g.
Moments about the wedge (rod's own weight neglected): $(M-500)\times2=200\times25$, so $M=3000$ g $=3$ kg.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin solid disk of 1 kg is rotating along its diameter axis at the speed of 1800 rpm. By applying an external torque of $25\pi$ Nm for 40s, the speed increases to 2100 rpm. The diameter of the disk is __________ m.
questions.sol:
$\Delta\omega=300$ rpm $=10\pi$ rad/s. Angular impulse: $\tau t=I\,\Delta\omega$, so $25\pi\times40=I\times10\pi$ and $I=100$ kg m$^2$.
About a diameter $I=\dfrac{MR^2}{4}$: $R^2=400$, $R=20$ m, so the diameter is 40 m.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
A sample of a liquid is kept at 1 atm. It is compressed to 5 atm which leads to change of volume of 0.8 cm$^3$. If the bulk modulus of the liquid is 2 GPa, the initial volume of the liquid was __________ litre.
(Take 1 atm $=10^5$ Pa)
questions.sol: $B=\dfrac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$, so $V=\dfrac{B\,\Delta V}{\Delta P}=\dfrac{2\times10^9\times0.8\times10^{-6}}{4\times10^5}=4\times10^{-3}$ m$^3=4$ litre.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate area 4 cm$^2$ and separation of $(d)$ 1.77 mm, is filled with uniform dielectric materials with dielectric constants (3 and 5)as shown in figure. Another capacitor of capacitance 7.5 pF is connected in parallel with it. The effective capacitance of this combination is __________ pF.
(Given $\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ F/m)
questions.sol:
The two layers, each of thickness $\dfrac d2$, are in series: $C=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{\frac{d}{2}\left(\frac15+\frac13\right)}=\dfrac{15}{4}\cdot\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}$.
$\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}=\dfrac{8.85\times10^{-12}\times4\times10^{-4}}{1.77\times10^{-3}}=2$ pF, so $C=7.5$ pF.
In parallel with 7.5 pF: $15$ pF.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electron is released from rest near an infinite non-conducting sheet of uniform charge density '$-\sigma$' .The rate of change of de-Broglie wave length associated with the electron varies inversely as $n^{th}$ power of time. The numerical value of n is __________.
questions.sol:
The field of an infinite sheet is uniform, so the electron has constant acceleration $a$ and $v=at$.
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{mat}\propto t^{-1}$, so $\dfrac{d\lambda}{dt}\propto t^{-2}$: $n=2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Correct statements for an element with atomic number 9 are
A. There can be 5 electrons for which $m_s=+\dfrac12$ and 4 electrons for which $m_s=-\dfrac12$
B. There is only one electron in $p_z$ orbital.
C. The last electron goes to orbital with $n=2$ and $l=1$.
D. The sum of angular nodes of all the atomic orbitals is 1.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Fluorine: $1s^22s^22p^5$, with one unpaired electron.
A: 4 pairs plus one unpaired electron, so 5 and 4 is possible. Correct.
B: the unpaired electron need not be in $p_z$; $p_z$ may hold two. Not correct.
C: the last electron enters a $2p$ orbital ($n=2$, $l=1$). Correct.
D: each of the three occupied $2p$ orbitals has one angular node and $s$ orbitals have none, so the sum is 3. Not correct.

questions.text: Which of the following binary mixture does not show the behaviour of minimum boiling azeotropes?
questions.sol:
Minimum boiling azeotropes come from positive deviation from Raoult's law (weaker attractions in the mixture).
Phenol and aniline form strong O-H$\cdots$N hydrogen bonds with each other: negative deviation, giving a maximum boiling azeotrope instead.

questions.text:
$\mathrm{HA}(aq)\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{H}^+(aq)+\mathrm{A}^-(aq)$
The freezing point depression of a 0.1 m aqueous solution of a monobasic weak acid HA is 0.20 °C. The dissociation constant for the acid is
Given : $K_f(\mathrm{H_2O})=1.8$ K kg mol$^{-1}$, molality $\equiv$ molarity
questions.sol:
$\Delta T_f=iK_fm$: $0.20=i\times1.8\times0.1$, so $i=\dfrac{10}{9}$ and $\alpha=i-1=\dfrac19$.
$K_a=\dfrac{c\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}=\dfrac{0.1\times(1/81)}{8/9}=\dfrac{1}{720}\approx1.38\times10^{-3}$.

questions.text: In a first order decomposition reaction, the time taken for the decomposition of reactant to one fourth and one eighth of its initial concentration are $t_1$ and $t_2$ (s), respectively. The ratio $t_1/t_2$ will be:
questions.sol:
For first order, $t=\dfrac1k\ln\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]}$: $t_1=\dfrac{\ln4}{k}=\dfrac{2\ln2}{k}$ and $t_2=\dfrac{3\ln2}{k}$ (two and three half-lives).
$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2}=\dfrac23$.

questions.text:
The number of species from the following that are involved in $sp^3d^2$ hybridization is
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{SF_6}$, $\mathrm{[CrF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$, $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$
questions.note: NTA's final key accepts both option (1), 4, and option (4), 3. The count of 3 treats $\mathrm{[CrF_6]^{3-}}$ as $d^2sp^3$; the count of 4 includes it as $sp^3d^2$.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{SF_6}$: S uses $3s$, $3p$ and two $3d$ orbitals, $sp^3d^2$.
$\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^6$) and $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^4$) with weak-field ligands are high-spin outer-orbital complexes, $sp^3d^2$.
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ are inner-orbital $d^2sp^3$; $\mathrm{[CrF_6]^{3-}}$ ($d^3$) has two empty $3d$ orbitals and is $d^2sp^3$ whatever the ligand.
So 3 species.

questions.text: The atomic number of the element from the following with lowest 1$^{st}$ ionisation enthalpy is :
questions.sol: 19 (K) and 87 (Fr) are alkali metals, 35 is Br and 32 is Ge. Ionisation enthalpy is lowest for the alkali metals and falls down the group, so Fr (87) has the lowest value.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : $\mathrm{H_2Se}$ is more acidic than $\mathrm{H_2Te}$
Statement II : $\mathrm{H_2Se}$ has higher bond enthalpy for dissociation than $\mathrm{H_2Te}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Down group 16 the E-H bond becomes longer and weaker, so the H-Se bond is stronger than the H-Te bond (II true).
Because the H-Te bond breaks more easily, $\mathrm{H_2Te}$ is the stronger acid (I false).

questions.text: The correct decreasing order of spin only magnetic moment values (BM) of $\mathrm{Cu^+}$, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ ions is :
questions.sol:
Unpaired electrons: $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ ($3d^4$) 4, $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ ($3d^3$) 3, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ($3d^9$) 1, $\mathrm{Cu^+}$ ($3d^{10}$) 0.
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ rises with $n$: $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}>Cr^{3+}>Cu^{2+}>Cu^+}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : A homoleptic octahedral complex, formed using monodentate ligands, will not show stereoisomerism
Statement II : cis- and trans - platin are heteroleptic complexes of Pd.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{[MA_6]}$ all six positions are equivalent, so there are no geometrical or optical isomers (I true).
Cisplatin and transplatin, $\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]}$, are heteroleptic complexes of platinum, not palladium (II false).

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I (Complex/ Species)LIST-II (Shape & magnetic moment)
A. $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$I. Tetrahedral, 2.8 BM
B. $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$II. Square planar, 0 BM
C. $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$III. Tetrahedral, 0 BM
D. $\mathrm{[MnBr_4]^{2-}}$IV. Tetrahedral, 5.9 BM
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: Ni(0), $3d^{10}$, $sp^3$: tetrahedral, 0 BM (III).
B: Ni(II) with strong-field $\mathrm{CN^-}$, $dsp^2$: square planar, 0 BM (II).
C: Ni(II) with weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, $sp^3$, two unpaired electrons: tetrahedral, 2.8 BM (I).

1,2-dibromocyclooctane $\xrightarrow[\text{(ii) NaNH}_2\text{; (iii) Hg}^{2+}/\text{H}^+\text{; (iv) Zn-Hg}/\text{H}^+]{\text{(i) KOH (alc.)}}$ P (major product)
'P' is

Clemmensen reduction (Zn-Hg/HCl) turns C=O into $\mathrm{CH_2}$: P is cyclooctane, option (3).

$\mathrm{Br_2/Fe}$ brominates the ring at the para position (the ethyl group is ortho/para directing).

questions.text:
Which one of the following reactions will not lead to the desired ether formation in major proportion ?
(iso-Bu $\Rightarrow$ isobutyl, sec-Bu $\Rightarrow$ sec-butyl, nPr $\Rightarrow$ n-propyl, $^t$Bu $\Rightarrow$ tert-butyl, Et $\Rightarrow$ ethyl)
questions.sol:
Williamson synthesis works well when the halide is methyl or primary ($\mathrm{S_N2}$).
In option (2) the halide is secondary (sec-butyl bromide) and the alkoxide is a strong base, so elimination to butenes dominates and the ether is not the major product.
Options (1), (3) and (4) use $\mathrm{CH_3Br}$, n-PrBr and EtBr and give the ethers.

questions.text: When the compound shown in the figure undergoes intramolecular aldol condensation, the major product formed is :
questions.sol:
The compound is 6-oxoheptanal, $\mathrm{CH_3CO(CH_2)_4CHO}$.
The enolate formed at the ring-side $\mathrm{CH_2}$ of the ketone (C-5) attacks the aldehyde carbon (C-1), closing a five-membered ring; dehydration gives the conjugated enone.
Product: 1-acetylcyclopentene (cyclopent-1-en-1-yl methyl ketone), option (3).

'B' gives effervescence with aq $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$.

Identify A, B and C from the following.

Alkaline hydrolysis and acidification give benzoic acid (B), which liberates $\mathrm{CO_2}$ from $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$.

20 mL of sodium iodide solution gave 4.74 g silver iodide when treated with excess of silver nitrate solution. The molarity of the sodium iodide solution is __________ M. (Nearest Integer value)

Molarity $=\dfrac{0.0202}{0.020}\approx1$ M.

questions.text: The energy of an electron in first Bohr orbit of H-atom is $-13.6$ eV. The magnitude of energy value of electron in the first excited state of $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$ is __________ eV (nearest integer value)
questions.sol:
$E_n=-13.6\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$ eV. For $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$, $Z=4$, and the first excited state is $n=2$: $E=-13.6\times\dfrac{16}{4}=-54.4$ eV.
Magnitude $\approx54$ eV.

questions.text:
Resonance in $\mathrm{X_2Y}$ can be represented as
The enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{X_2Y}$ $\left(\mathrm{X{\equiv}X(g)}+\dfrac12\mathrm{Y{=}Y(g)}\rightarrow\mathrm{X_2Y(g)}\right)$ is 80 kJ mol$^{-1}$. The magnitude of resonance energy of $\mathrm{X_2Y}$ is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (nearest integer value)
Given : Bond energies of $\mathrm{X{\equiv}X}$, $\mathrm{X{=}X}$, $\mathrm{Y{=}Y}$ and $\mathrm{X{=}Y}$ are 940, 410, 500 and 602 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively.
valence X: 3 , Y: 2
questions.sol:
Use the structure $\mathrm{X{=}X{=}Y}$, whose bond energies are all given.
Calculated $\Delta_fH=$ (bonds broken) $-$ (bonds formed) $=\left(940+\dfrac{500}{2}\right)-(410+602)=1190-1012=178$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
The observed value is 80 kJ mol$^{-1}$, so resonance stabilises the molecule by $178-80=98$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The equilibrium constant for decomposition of $\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$
$\mathrm{H_2O(g)\rightleftharpoons H_2(g)+\dfrac12O_2(g)}$ ($\Delta G^\circ=92.34$ kJ mol$^{-1}$)
is $8.0\times10^{-3}$ at 2300 K and total pressure at equilibrium is 1 bar. Under this condition, the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) of water is __________ $\times10^{-2}$ (nearest integer value).
[Assume $\alpha$ is negligible with respect to 1]
questions.sol:
Mole fractions (total about 1 mol for 1 mol water): $\mathrm{H_2O}$ $1-\alpha\approx1$, $\mathrm{H_2}$ $\alpha$, $\mathrm{O_2}$ $\dfrac\alpha2$; total pressure 1 bar.
$K_p=\dfrac{\alpha\left(\frac\alpha2\right)^{1/2}}{1}=\dfrac{\alpha^{3/2}}{\sqrt2}=8.0\times10^{-3}$, so $\alpha^{3/2}=1.13\times10^{-2}$ and $\alpha\approx0.050=5\times10^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following half cell reaction
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}(aq)+6e^-+14H^+(aq)\longrightarrow2Cr^{3+}(aq)+7H_2O(l)}$
The reaction was conducted with the ratio of $\dfrac{[\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}]^2}{[\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}]}=10^{-6}$. The pH value at which the EMF of the half cell will become zero is __________. (nearest integer value)
[Given : standard half cell reduction potential $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}, H^+/Cr^{3+}}}=1.33$ V, $\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.059$ V.]
